topics.title: Fraction recap, the area model and cancelling

learn.hook: Multiplying fractions can be drawn! Shade a square one way, shade it again the other way — the overlap is the answer.
points: Equivalent fractions: multiply or divide the numerator and denominator by the same number: 2/3 = 4/6 = 8/12.
Lowest terms: divide top and bottom by their HCF: 18/24 → divide by 6 → 3/4.
Area model: in a unit square, shade 2/3 of the width and 3/4 of the height. The overlap is 6 of the 12 small boxes: 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2.
Cancelling: in 4/9 × 3/8, cancel 4 with 8 and 3 with 9 first: 1/3 × 1/2 = 1/6.
Cancelling before multiplying keeps the numbers small and gives the answer in lowest terms.

example.q: Use the area model to find 2/3 × 3/4.
steps: Split the square into 3 columns and 4 rows: 12 small boxes

learn.reallife: If a garden plot is 2/3 of a field's width and 3/4 of its length, the plot is half the field — the area model shows it.

quiz.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 3/4?
quiz.mistake: Adds the same number to top and bottom

quiz.q: Write 18/24 in lowest terms.
quiz.explain: The HCF of 18 and 24 is 6. 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4.
quiz.mistake: Divides by a factor that is not common

quiz.q: A unit square is split into 3 columns and 5 rows. 2 columns and 4 rows are shaded. What fraction of the square is in the overlap?
quiz.explain: The overlap is 2 × 4 = 8 boxes out of 3 × 5 = 15: 2/3 × 4/5 = 8/15.
quiz.mistake: Adds the shaded columns and rows

quiz.q: In the area model for 3/4 × 1/2, how many small boxes is the square split into?
quiz.explain: 4 parts one way and 2 parts the other way: 4 × 2 = 8 boxes.
quiz.mistake: Adds the denominators

quiz.explain: Cancel 4 with 8 (→ 1 and 2) and 3 with 9 (→ 1 and 3): 1/3 × 1/2 = 1/6.
quiz.mistake: Adds numerators and denominators
Cancels two numbers that are both on top

quiz.q: Write 35/56 in lowest terms.
quiz.explain: The HCF of 35 and 56 is 7. 35 ÷ 7 = 5 and 56 ÷ 7 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Divides only the numerator

quiz.q: Fill the box: 5/7 = ☐/42
quiz.explain: 7 × 6 = 42, so multiply the top by 6 too: 5 × 6 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Adds 35 to the numerator because 7 + 35 = 42

teach.ask: Gappu must find 4/9 × 3/8 but hates big numbers. What trick can Gappu use?
teach.praise: Smart! Gappu cancelled first and got 1/6 in one step.
teach.nudge: Which top and bottom numbers share a common factor?

learn.hook: Half of half a laddoo — is that a quarter? Multiplying fractions answers questions like this!
points: Whole × fraction: 3 × 2/5 means 2/5 + 2/5 + 2/5 = 6/5.
'Of' means multiply: 1/4 of 24 = 1/4 × 24 = 6.
Fraction × fraction: multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators: 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2.
You can cancel common factors before multiplying to keep numbers small.
Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 gives an answer smaller than the number you started with.
learn.reallife: Recipes, discounts and sharing sweets all use 'fraction of' — like 3/4 of a kg of jalebis.

quiz.q: What is 3 × 2/5?
quiz.explain: 3 × 2/5 = 2/5 + 2/5 + 2/5 = 6/5. Only the numerator is multiplied by 3.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies both the numerator and the denominator by 3

quiz.q: Riya has 24 laddoos. She gives 1/4 of them to her neighbour. How many does she give?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 24 by 4 instead of finding a quarter

quiz.q: What is 2/3 × 3/4?
quiz.mistake: Adds the numerators and denominators instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Arjun walks 3/4 km every day. How far does he walk in 6 days?
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 and 3/4 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Which is true about 1/2 × 1/3?
options: It is 1/6, which is smaller than both fractions
quiz.explain: 1/2 × 1/3 = 1/6. Taking a part of a part gives something smaller than both.
quiz.mistake: Adds the denominators instead of multiplying them

quiz.q: Meena has ₹60 and spends 2/5 of it on a storybook. How much does the book cost?
quiz.mistake: Finds only 1/5 of the money

quiz.q: A card is 3/4 m long and 2/3 m wide. What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two lengths instead of multiplying

quiz.q: What is 1/2 of 1/2 of 40?
quiz.mistake: Takes half only once

teach.ask: Gappu wants to find 2/3 × 3/4. How do you multiply two fractions?
teach.praise: Yippee! Tops times tops, bottoms times bottoms — Gappu got 1/2!
teach.nudge: What do we do with the numerators and with the denominators?

topics.title: Properties of fraction multiplication and word problems

learn.hook: Six saplings planted 3/4 m apart — how far is it from the first to the last? Careful, it's not 6 × 3/4!
points: Commutative: 2/3 × 3/5 = 3/5 × 2/3 — the order doesn't matter.
Associative: (1/2 × 2/3) × 3/4 = 1/2 × (2/3 × 3/4) — the grouping doesn't matter.
A tap filling 2/5 of a tank per hour fills 2/5 × 5/2 = 1 whole tank in 2 1/2 hours.
6 saplings in a row have 5 gaps; at 3/4 m each, the first to last is 5 × 3/4 = 3 3/4 m.

example.q: A garden plot is 2 1/2 m long and 1 1/2 m wide. Find its area.

learn.reallife: Farmers sharing land, gardeners spacing plants and plumbers timing tanks all multiply fractions.

games.title: Property and problem check

quiz.q: A tap fills 2/5 of a tank every hour. What part of the tank does it fill in 2 1/2 hours?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of multiplying

quiz.q: A plot is 2 1/2 m long and 1 1/2 m wide. What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the whole parts and the fraction parts separately

quiz.q: 6 saplings are planted in a row, 3/4 m apart. How far is the first sapling from the last?
quiz.mistake: Counts 6 gaps instead of 5

quiz.q: A farmer owns 3/4 of an acre and gives 2/3 of it to his daughter. What part of an acre does she get?
quiz.mistake: Adds the fractions instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Which property is shown by 3/7 × 2/9 = 2/9 × 3/7?
quiz.explain: The two fractions are swapped and the product stays the same.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up swapping with grouping

quiz.q: Find 3/4 × 5/7 + 3/4 × 2/7 using the distributive property.
quiz.mistake: Finds only the first product

quiz.q: Find (1/2 × 4/5) × 5/8 by grouping smartly.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only two of the three fractions

quiz.q: Ria cycles 3 1/3 km every day. How far does she cycle in 6 days?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the whole part by 6

teach.ask: Gappu planted 5 saplings 1/2 m apart and says the row is 2 1/2 m long. Is Gappu right?
teach.praise: Yes! 4 gaps × 1/2 m = 2 m — Gappu fixed the row.
teach.nudge: How many gaps are there between 5 saplings?

topics.title: Division as the inverse; choosing the right operation

learn.hook: 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12? Check it backwards: 1/4 × 12 = 3. Division just undoes multiplication!
points: Division undoes multiplication: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 because 3 × 4 = 12.
For fractions too: 2 ÷ 1/3 asks '1/3 × ☐ = 2?' The answer is 6.
Always check a division by multiplying back: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 6 because 1/8 × 6 = 6/8 = 3/4.
'Of', 'each ... for n' → multiply. 'How many ... in', 'share equally' → divide.
Before calculating a word problem, choose the expression — then check that the answer makes sense.
learn.reallife: When a recipe says '3/4 cup per batch' and you have 3 cups, dividing tells you how many batches you can make.

quiz.q: Which multiplication checks that 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12?
quiz.explain: Division is the inverse of multiplication: divisor × answer = number divided.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the wrong pair of numbers

quiz.q: Find the missing number: 1/3 × ☐ = 5
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 5 by 1/3 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Find the missing number: 2/5 × ☐ = 4
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 4 × 2/5

quiz.q: Find the missing number: 3/4 × ☐ = 3/8
quiz.mistake: Divides the wrong way round

quiz.q: A 12 m rope is cut into pieces of 3/4 m. Which expression gives the number of pieces?
quiz.explain: 'How many 3/4 m pieces in 12 m' is a division.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies because the word 'pieces' sounds like 'of'

quiz.q: Each glass holds 1/4 L. Which expression gives the juice needed for 10 glasses?
quiz.explain: 10 glasses each holding 1/4 L is 10 × 1/4 = 2 1/2 L.
quiz.mistake: Divides because a fraction is involved

quiz.q: The winner gets 3/5 of a ₹500 prize. Which expression gives the winner's share?
quiz.mistake: Divides when 'of' is used

quiz.q: 2/3 of a cake is shared equally by 4 children. Which expression gives each child's part of the whole cake?
quiz.explain: Sharing equally among 4 is dividing by 4: 2/3 ÷ 4 = 1/6.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by the number of children

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 2 ÷ 1/3 should be smaller than 2. How can Gappu check the real answer?

learn.hook: How can 3 ÷ 1/4 be 12 — bigger than 3? Dividing by a fraction is full of surprises!
points: Dividing asks 'how many of these fit in?': 3 ÷ 1/4 asks how many quarters fit in 3. Answer: 12.
The reciprocal of a fraction is the fraction turned upside down: the reciprocal of 3/5 is 5/3.
To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 3/4 × 8/1 = 6.
A fraction ÷ a whole number: 1/2 ÷ 3 = 1/2 × 1/3 = 1/6.
Dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a bigger answer. The number 0 has no reciprocal.

example.q: How many 1/4 kg packets of peanuts can be filled from 3 kg?

learn.reallife: Cutting a long ribbon into equal 3/4 m pieces, or filling 1/2 L bottles from a big can, means dividing by a fraction.

games.title: Division truths
items: Dividing by 1/2 is the same as multiplying by 2.
The reciprocal of 1/2 is 2.
8 ÷ 1/4 = 8 × 4 = 32. There are 32 quarters in 8.
The reciprocal of 1 is 1.
1 × 1 = 1, so 1 is its own reciprocal.
Dividing a number by a fraction less than 1 always makes it smaller.
It makes it bigger: 6 ÷ 1/2 = 12.
0 has a reciprocal.
No number times 0 gives 1, so 0 has no reciprocal.

quiz.q: What is the reciprocal of 4/9?
quiz.explain: Turn the fraction upside down: 4/9 becomes 9/4. Check: 4/9 × 9/4 = 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the reciprocal is the same fraction

quiz.q: How many halves are there in 5?
quiz.explain: 5 ÷ 1/2 = 5 × 2 = 10. Each whole has 2 halves, and 5 wholes have 10.
quiz.mistake: Divides 5 by 2 instead of dividing by 1/2

quiz.q: Kabir has 3 kg of rice and fills packets of 1/4 kg each. How many packets does he fill?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 3 by 1/4 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Find 2/3 ÷ 4.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 4 instead of dividing

quiz.q: What is 3/4 ÷ 3/8?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the fractions without flipping the second one

quiz.q: A ribbon is 7 1/2 m long. It is cut into pieces of 3/4 m. How many pieces are there?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies instead of dividing

quiz.q: Aisha shares 2/5 of a cake equally between 2 friends. What part of the whole cake does each friend get?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 2 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Which gives the biggest answer?
quiz.mistake: Thinks division always makes a number smaller

teach.ask: Gappu must divide 3/4 by 1/8. What is the trick for dividing by a fraction?
teach.praise: Woohoo! 3/4 × 8 = 6. Gappu found six 1/8 pieces in 3/4!
teach.nudge: After you flip the second fraction, what do you do?

learn.hook: Cooking for more guests, sharing pocket money, cutting ribbons — fractions are hiding in all of them!
points: 'Of' or 'part of' usually means multiply: 2/3 of 30 = 20.
'How many … fit in' or 'share equally' usually means divide.
Change mixed numbers like 2 1/2 into improper fractions (5/2) before multiplying or dividing.
Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 makes things smaller; dividing by it makes things bigger.
After solving, check that your answer makes sense for the story.

example.q: A recipe for 4 people needs 3/4 cup of sugar. How much sugar is needed for 6 people?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers sell 1/4 kg and 1/2 kg packets, and families scale recipes up for Diwali guests — all fraction maths!

quiz.q: A recipe for 4 people needs 3/4 cup of sugar. How much sugar is needed for 6 people?
quiz.explain: For 1 person: 3/4 ÷ 4 = 3/16 cup. For 6 people: 3/16 × 6 = 18/16 = 1 1/8 cups.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 3/4 by 6 without first finding the amount for one person

quiz.q: A train goes 60 km in one hour. How far does it go in 2 1/2 hours at the same speed?
quiz.mistake: Ignores the half hour or divides instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Aisha reads 2/5 of a 150-page book on Sunday. How many pages are left to read?
quiz.mistake: Gives the pages she read instead of the pages left

quiz.q: Harpreet pours a 2 L jug of lassi into glasses that hold 1/5 L each. How many glasses does she fill?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 2 by 1/5 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Joseph has a 5 m rope. He uses 1/2 of it, and then 1/3 of what is left. How much rope remains?
quiz.explain: After using half, 5/2 m is left. 1/3 of 5/2 is 5/6. Remaining: 5/2 − 5/6 = 15/6 − 5/6 = 10/6 = 1 2/3 m.
quiz.mistake: Takes 1/3 of the whole rope instead of 1/3 of what is left

quiz.q: A family eats 3/4 kg of rice every day. How much rice do they eat in a week?
quiz.mistake: Adds 7 and 3/4 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: ₹240 is shared. Riya gets 1/3 of it and Joseph gets 1/4 of it. How much money is left?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts only one person's share

quiz.q: Kabir multiplied 12 by 2/3 and got 18. Is his answer reasonable?
options: Yes — multiplying always makes a number bigger
No — multiplying by a fraction less than 1 should give less than 12
quiz.explain: 2/3 is less than 1, so 2/3 of 12 must be less than 12. The correct answer is 8.
quiz.mistake: Thinks multiplying always increases a number

teach.ask: Gappu is solving fraction stories. How does he know when to multiply and when to divide?
teach.praise: Brilliant! 'Of' means multiply, 'how many fit' means divide. Gappu is a fraction detective!
teach.nudge: Which word in a story tells you to multiply?

topics.title: Halving patterns, product puzzles and Lilavati

learn.hook: (1 − 1/2)(1 − 1/3)(1 − 1/4)... up to 1/100 — almost everything cancels and the answer is just 1/100!
points: Repeated halving: shade 1/2 of a square, then half of what's left, then half again: 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 = 7/8 is shaded, 1/8 is not.
Repeated splitting: if an ant covers half the remaining distance each minute, after 3 minutes 1/2 × 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/8 of the distance is left.
Bhaskara II wrote Lilavati in the 12th century. It has fraction puzzles about dramma coins and cowries.
In one puzzle a miser gives a beggar 1/16 of 1/5 of 1/4 of 1/2 of 2/3 of 3/4 of a dramma — and 1 dramma = 1,280 cowries.

steps: Each numerator cancels the denominator before it
Only 1 on top and 10 at the bottom are left

learn.reallife: Cutting a sheet of paper in half again and again, or sharing the last piece of cake, shows how fast halves get tiny.

games.title: Halves and products
items: Halving again and again, the shaded part becomes more than 1
It gets closer and closer to 1 but never goes over.
Bhaskara II wrote Lilavati
It is a 12th-century book of arithmetic.
It is 1/5.

quiz.q: Shade 1/2 of a square, then half of the unshaded part, then half of what is still unshaded. What fraction is shaded now?
quiz.mistake: Gives the unshaded part instead

quiz.q: Keep halving the unshaded part of a square. After 4 halvings, what fraction is still unshaded?
quiz.explain: Each step halves the unshaded part: 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16.
quiz.mistake: Stops one step early

quiz.q: An ant is 16 m from a tree. Each minute it covers half of the distance that is left. How far is it from the tree after 3 minutes?
quiz.explain: Left after each minute: 8 m, 4 m, 2 m. That is 1/8 of 16 m.
quiz.mistake: Gives the distance walked instead of the distance left

quiz.q: The same ant (16 m away, half the remaining distance each minute): how far has it walked after 3 minutes?
quiz.explain: It is 2 m from the tree, so it has walked 16 − 2 = 14 m (8 + 4 + 2).
quiz.mistake: Gives the distance left
Multiplies 1/2 × 1/3 × 1/4 instead
Stops the pattern at the wrong number

quiz.q: Lilavati puzzle: 1/16 of 1/5 of 1/4 of 1/2 of 2/3 of 3/4 of a dramma is 1/☐ of a dramma. What number goes in the box?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one of the fractions, or forgets to simplify 6/7680

quiz.q: If 1 dramma = 1,280 cowries, how many cowries did the miser give the beggar (1/1280 of a dramma)?
quiz.explain: 1/1280 × 1,280 = 1 cowrie — a very small gift indeed!
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of cowries in a whole dramma
